finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of ownership. The ownership check calls authorized(), which only returns a boolean, and the result is discarded, so no 403 is ever thrown. Any authenticated user can delete other users' projects by id.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (req.user set) who knows or enumerates a project id, supplied via the :id path parameter (api.js:16-17).
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, a destructive operation on a project owned by someone else.

trace.note: Route handler registered for DELETE /projects/:id with no route-level guard.
Project loaded by req.params.id with no owner or tenant scoping.
authorized(req.user, project) is called as a bare statement. It returns true or false, and the return value is ignored, so it cannot block the request.
authorized() returns resource.ownerId === user.id || user.isAdmin === true. It does not throw, unlike authorize() at lines 4-10.
Project is deleted and 204 is returned (line 20).

finding.guards_checked: Compared with the sibling PUT route (api.js:23-28), which uses the throwing authorize() helper and correctly blocks non-owners. Confirmed authorized() has no side effect that enforces the check and the DELETE handler has no other check in this file. Could not check upstream middleware (req.user population, any global auth guard, req.store tenant scoping) because only api.js is present.

verdict.guard_found: Only api.js:18 `authorized(req.user, project)`, which returns a boolean that is discarded as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. The throwing `authorize()` (api.js:4-10) is not called on the DELETE route; it is only used by the PUT route at api.js:25. No route-level guard is registered at api.js:16. Upstream middleware (req.user population, global auth, req.store tenant scoping) is not in the provided files and could not be checked.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:18 calls `authorized()` (which returns a bool, api.js:12-14) as a bare statement, so its result never gates `req.store.projects.delete(project.id)` at api.js:19, and any authenticated user can delete another owner's project by id; the only residual uncertainty is unseen upstream middleware, which would have to enforce ownership per-id for this to be refuted.
